findings.description: File lock created with insecure world-readable permissions (644)
findings.reasoning: The os.open() call uses self._context.mode which defaults to 0o644 (world-readable). This creates lock files with permissions rw-r--r--, allowing other users on the system to read the lock file contents. In multi-user environments or shared systems, this could expose sensitive information or allow unauthorized access to lock state.

evidence.dataflow_analysis: The mode parameter comes from self._context.mode which is initialized with default value 0o644 in FileLockMeta.__call__ method. This default value creates files with world-readable permissions.
evidence.notes: Default mode is 0o644 as seen in FileLockMeta.__call__ at line 75: mode: int = 0o644. This is insecure for lock files that may contain sensitive information or need to be protected from other users.
